learningObjectives: Link TestSheet Instances to Requirements by drag-and-drop.
Explain the difference between a TestCase-Substitute link and a TestCase link.
Explain how ExecutionLists connect to RequirementSets to build a project dashboard.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Why link TestCase Design back to Requirements

elements.description: Linking gives an early-stage overview of how much of the planned test design work maps onto the defined Requirements — how much of the project has actually been thought through and structured, before a single physical TestCase is built.

Drag Instances from the TestSheet onto their matching Requirement. If every Instance on the TestSheet belongs to that Requirement, the whole TestSheet can be dragged at once. If only some Instances are in scope right now — for example, only the ones planned for the current sprint — select and drag just those individual Instances instead.

The result of linking Instances to a Requirement before any physical TestCase exists. It's a placeholder link showing how many TestCases will eventually need to be built in the TestCase section to cover that Requirement.

Once the physical TestCases are actually built (in the blue TestCase section) and linked to the same Requirements, the earlier TestCase-Substitute links become full TestCase links — reflecting real, executable TestCases instead of a planning placeholder.

bulletPoints: Drag the whole TestSheet when all its Instances belong to one Requirement; drag individual Instances when only a subset does (e.g. this sprint's data).
TestCase-Substitute link = planned but not yet built. TestCase link = the real, physical TestCase, now linked.

elements.term: Rule of thumb: one TestSheet per Requirement
elements.description: A TestSheet should contain all the TestCases needed to cover its Requirement. In sprint-based projects this can differ slightly — one TestSheet might accumulate TestCases created across multiple sprints for the same Requirement, rather than being rebuilt each sprint.

elements.term: ExecutionLists link to RequirementSets, not individual Requirements
elements.description: When ExecutionLists are created, they are linked to the whole RequirementSet rather than to a single Requirement. This rolls up progress across the entire set: which TestCases have been defined, which Requirements are actively being worked on, how far along the project is, and — once executions have actually run — which passed and which failed.

elements.text: Together, this chain (TestSheet → Requirement → TestCase → ExecutionList → RequirementSet) is what turns the Requirements section into a live project dashboard inside Tosca Commander.

bulletPoints: ExecutionList links to the RequirementSet level — giving whole-project visibility, not just one Requirement's status.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing TestCase-Substitute links with TestCase links
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming both terms describe the same thing at different points in the process.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A TestCase-Substitute link exists before the physical TestCase is built — it's a placeholder showing planned coverage. Once the physical TestCase is built and linked, it becomes a full TestCase link.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming ExecutionLists link to individual Requirements
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting to link an ExecutionList directly to one Requirement for granular tracking.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ExecutionLists link to the whole RequirementSet, giving a rolled-up view of progress and execution results across every Requirement in that set.

examPitfalls.title: Always dragging the entire TestSheet onto a Requirement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Dragging the full TestSheet even when only a subset of its Instances (e.g. this sprint's) are actually in scope.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When only some Instances belong to the current scope, select and drag just those individual Instances rather than the whole TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester drags Instances from a TestSheet onto a Requirement before any physical TestCase has been built. What kind of link is created?
practiceQuiz.hint: This link is a planning placeholder, not the real thing yet.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Linking Instances to a Requirement before the physical TestCase exists creates a TestCase-Substitute link — showing how many TestCases will eventually need to be built to cover that Requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: At what level does an ExecutionList link, in order to show overall project progress?
practiceQuiz.hint: This is what makes it a project-wide dashboard rather than a one-Requirement view.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionLists link to the entire RequirementSet, rolling up execution results and coverage across all of its Requirements — giving whole-project visibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Only 4 of a TestSheet's 12 Instances are planned for the current sprint. What is the correct way to link them to their Requirement?

options.text: Drag the entire TestSheet onto the Requirement, since partial linking isn't possible.
Select and drag only the 4 relevant Instances onto the Requirement.
Wait until all 12 Instances are ready before linking any of them.
Duplicate the TestSheet and delete the other 8 Instances first.

practiceQuiz.hint: Drag-and-drop linking works at the Instance level, not only the whole-TestSheet level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Individual Instances can be selected and dragged onto a Requirement when only a subset is currently in scope — there's no need to link the whole TestSheet or wait for every Instance to be ready.

quickRecap.value: Drag Instances (or the whole TestSheet) from TestCase Design onto the matching Requirement.
Placeholder link, created before the physical TestCase exists.
Replaces the Substitute link once the real TestCase is built and linked.
Rule of thumb — one TestSheet per Requirement, containing all its TestCases.
Links to the whole RequirementSet — giving a rolled-up, project-wide progress dashboard.
